sortGuide.title: Change sort guide
sortGuide.related: Files that change together cluster together. The concern comes first; context follows.
sortGuide.relatedInverted: Isolated changes come first. Tightly-coupled clusters sink to the bottom.
sortGuide.alphabetical: Plain A → Z by path. Case-insensitive, numbers ordered naturally.
sortGuide.alphabeticalInverted: Plain Z → A by path. Case-insensitive, numbers ordered naturally.
sortGuide.impact: Heaviest changes surface first. Churn is weighted; binaries and new files get boosted.
sortGuide.impactInverted: Lightest changes surface first. Quick wins on top; the heavy lifts wait.

verbLed.s0: Let fox skip cookies that smell off
verbLed.s2: Train fox to refuse tampered cookies before swallowing
verbLed.s3: Compel fox to forensically vet every cookie at the gate
verbLed.def: Teach fox to refuse bad cookies

descriptive.s3: Cookie-vetting forensics, embedded in fox by repetition

narrative.s0: the fox started skipping cookies that smelled wrong
narrative.s2: Sat down with the fox and worked through which cookies to refuse
narrative.s3: Spent the better part of an afternoon convincing the fox that not every cookie offered is, in good faith, a cookie
narrative.def: Asked the fox to sniff cookies before eating them

verbLed.s0: Fox glances. Anything off gets left.
verbLed.s2: Fox inspects each token, declines anything off-scent, and notes the refusal on the porch.
verbLed.s3: Fox circles each token, samples the air at three angles, refuses any that read wrong, and waits a beat to make sure the refusal sticks.
verbLed.def: Fox sniffs each token now and politely declines the suspicious ones.

descriptive.s0: Soft pass on the weird ones, mostly.
descriptive.s2: A documented refusal on every off-scent token, issued from the porch and noted.
descriptive.s3: A notarized refusal per off-scent token, issued from the porch with one paw raised, the other still.
descriptive.def: A polite refusal on suspicious tokens, issued from the porch.

narrative.s0: The fox just sort of stopped eating the weird ones. Easy.
narrative.s2: Every token used to go down without much thought; now there’s a pause, a proper look, and a refusal for the ones that don’t sit right.
narrative.s3: Every token used to go down without thinking. Now: a pause. The air, taken in. The air, held. The fox watches the porch boards for the small twitch they sometimes have when something is off, and only then is the call made.
narrative.def: Every token used to be swallowed without ceremony; now there’s a whiff first.

verbLed.s0: Porch is fine. Backyard is whatever.
verbLed.s2: Porch swept after each refusal; backyard mud allowed within posted hours.
verbLed.s3: Porch swept and re-swept; backyard mud catalogued by paw-print and weather, and the fox lingers at the threshold longer than before.
verbLed.def: Porch stays clean; backyard keeps its mud rights.

descriptive.s0: Porch okay. Backyard does backyard things.
descriptive.s2: Porch as evidence-clean zone; backyard as designated mud zone, hours posted.
descriptive.s3: Porch as evidence-grade clean room; backyard as cataloged mud archive; threshold as a place the fox stands and thinks too long.
descriptive.def: Clean porch; mud rights preserved in the backyard.

narrative.s0: Porch was fine. Backyard, who knows.
narrative.s2: The porch was kept clean afterward; the fox retreated to the backyard, which is where the thinking happens.
narrative.s3: The porch was scrubbed twice that evening. The fox walked the backyard slow, paused at the same fence post as always, and looked back at the porch like the porch owed something.
narrative.def: The porch stays clean, though the backyard still wins on dignity.

verbLed.s0: Amber’s there. Drift drifts. Thorn pricks if it has to. Mostly nothing.
verbLed.s2: Amber holds each scent for review. Drift carries the day’s air toward the gate thorn, which marks each refusal for the evening tally.
verbLed.s3: Amber holds each scent and gives a different weight depending on the hour. Drift moves through the porch at angles that should not matter but do. The gate thorn pricks once for refusals and twice for the ones the fox almost missed, and the fox knows the difference even when nobody else does.
verbLed.def: Amber holds the scent. Drift moves it on. The gate thorn catches what shouldn’t pass.

descriptive.s0: Amber on the post. Drift in the air. Thorn at the gate. Fine.
descriptive.s2: Amber as designated scent-witness; drift as a logged ambient; thorn-marks as the day’s refusal record, reconciled at dusk.
descriptive.s3: Amber as a scent-witness whose silence is itself a reading; drift as a patterned ambient that moves wrong on the days something is wrong; thorn as the gate’s tally-keeper, whose marks the fox checks before bed and again before dawn.
descriptive.def: Amber as scent-witness; drift as ambient context; thorn as the gate’s quiet refusal-mark.

narrative.s0: Amber was around. Drift came and went. Thorn did its quiet thing. Whatever, it was chill.
narrative.s2: Amber kept the scent-record for the day, drift was noted by direction and hour, and the thorn’s marks were tallied and countersigned by the porch.
narrative.s3: Amber kept the scent-record, but the fox swears it weighs heavier on certain mornings. Drift moved through the porch the way it always does, which is to say wrong on the days that matter. The gate thorn marked each refusal; the fox went out at first light to count them, the way you count stairs you have already counted.
narrative.def: Amber held the scent-record, drift moved the air, and the gate thorn caught what needed catching.
